text:
andrew: heads-up — started seeing a small but consistent tail-latency bump on a subset of hosted nodes after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. not across all traffic, mostly client payloads with lots of tiny spans.

maria: ugh. any traces?

andrew: yeah attaching the critical bit. stack shows host CPU in parse/serialize during request ingress, before batching. KV cache evictions line up with the spike. hypothesis: coalesce/parsepath changed the write pattern causing extra copies + syscalls.

perf-bot: perf alert: 99p latency +18% on /v1/generate for requests with <256b tokens and >6 fragments (since deploy 3460000000).

ken: can you paste the snippet of the trace? small sample is fine.

andrew: here — note repeated `write()` syscalls and short-lived allocations:
```
# strace-ish excerpt (redacted)
write(3, "\x01\x02...", 128) = 128
write(3, "\x03\x04...", 64) = 64
poll([...], 100) = 0
malloc(64) = 0x7f8b1f000
free(0x7f8b1f000)

# host CPU shows parsepath_worker @ 35% (was 12% prior)
```

andrew: also see KV cache miss rate jumping from 2.1% -> 6.7% for these flows. evictions correlate with fragment count.

sara: interesting — could be the coalesce window forcing more fragmented writes (so smaller, more frequent KV touch) which in turn thrashes hot shards. Did selector change affect batching hints?

maria: yes we widened kernel choice to prefer slim kernels for low-token sequences — it reduces decode cost but the ingress path now sends more mini-chunks to the runtime. autoscaler config unchanged.

ken: two immediate hypotheses: 1) coalesce threshold + kernel hint combo increases syscall churn and prevents writev coalescing, 2) mini-chunks increase KV churn and reduce locality so kvcache hotset degrades.

andrew: agreed. quick repro: run a client that sends 10k requests of payloads with 8 fragments vs a single-frag payload, compare `writev` counts and kvcache hit%. I ran a smoke and saw ~3x write calls.

maria: can we try a mitigations matrix? suggestions:
- bump coalesce buffer time by 2ms only for low-token routes
- re-enable a small writev heuristic when kernel hint = slim
- pin kvcache shard affinity for these flows temporarily

ken: +1 to heuristic toggle first (lowest blast). also add a perf counter to expose `writev_calls` per-request.

perf-bot: note created perf ticket PERF-4792: "measure writev/write syscalls and kvcache eviction correlation for low-token multi-frag flows". tagging @eng-runtime.

andrew: i'll wire an A/B with the coalesce buffer change in canary cluster. if tail drops and eviction rate drops we ship. will post numbers in this thread.

sara: if that fails, we should consider changing kernel selection back to previous behavioral fallback for request shapes with >4 fragments.

maria: agreed. also drop a note in release notes to track regressions tied to kernel selection.

andrew: quick raw numbers from canary (5m window):
- baseline (pre-change): 99p=82ms, write_calls/request=1.4, kvcache_evictions/1k=2
- post-change (current): 99p=98ms, write_calls/request=3.9, kvcache_evictions/1k=7
- canary (coalesce +2ms): 99p=84ms, write_calls/request=1.6, kvcache_evictions/1k=2.5

ken: that's promising. can you run end-to-end CPU profile to confirm host parse CPU drops?

andrew: running now — profile shows parse/serialize CPU drop from 34% -> 14% on hosts with coalesce bump.

maria: ok let's roll coalesce tweak to 50% of hosts for 1h, monitor 99p and kvcache evictions. if green, stage rollout.

sara: and add a temporary rule in smart-routing to avoid selecting slim kernel for routes with fragment_count>6 until we confirm kvcache adaptation.

andrew: will do. logging follow-ups here. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — great catch.
